t: #2669 Count Artist Occurrences On Spotify Ranking List
o: A pure SQL aggregation: count rows per artist and order by count descending, name ascending. In the sample, DJ Khalid and Ed Sheeran each appear twice, Sia once. Note the requested column alias is `occurrences`.
k: ORDER BY occurrences DESC, artist ASC resolves ties alphabetically.

a.i: One pass grouping by artist; COUNT(*) counts ranking entries per artist, then sort by the alias.
s: Count rows per group as occurrences.
Order by occurrences DESC, then artist ASC.

c.python:
-- MySQL solution (this is a Database problem; SQL applies to all language slots)
SELECT artist, COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM Spotify
GROUP BY artist
ORDER BY occurrences DESC, artist ASC;

a.t: O(N log N) — aggregation plus sort by the engine
a.sp: O(A) groups for A distinct artists

a.i: Equivalent formulation computing the counts in a subquery and selecting from it — handy when you need further filtering (e.g., HAVING) or joins afterward.
s: Aggregate into a derived table with the alias.

c.python:
-- MySQL
SELECT artist, occurrences
FROM (
    SELECT artist, COUNT(*) AS occurrences
    FROM Spotify
    GROUP BY artist
) t
ORDER BY occurrences DESC, artist ASC;

w: COUNT(*) vs COUNT(column) matters only with NULLs; artist is presumably non-null here. Pitfall: ordering ties by name ascending is easy to forget. Follow-up: only artists with ≥ 2 appearances (add HAVING).
